questions.text: Which of the following is not an application of speech in affective computing?
According to Borden et al. (1994), “how it is said” refers to:
options: The linguistic meaning of the words

questions.text: Natural emotional speech databases primarily include:
Positive emotions always produce lower variability in pitch.
The Berlin Emotional Speech Database contains recordings of:
options: Professional actors producing emotional German sentences
North American speakers producing neutral statements
Patients and doctors in clinical settings
questions.correctAnswer: Professional actors producing emotional German sentences

questions.text: MFCCs are primarily used to represent:
Positive voices typically show which characteristic?
options: Low pitch and low formant frequencies
High loudness variability and high formant frequencies
questions.correctAnswer: High loudness variability and high formant frequencies

questions.text: A key problem with global normalization of f0 across all speakers is that it:
options: May blur emotional differences due to speaker-specific traits
questions.correctAnswer: May blur emotional differences due to speaker-specific traits
